messages:
leo: FYI — 11:03 UTC p95 jumped ~45ms -> ~720ms on runtime-serving-prod (approx 11:03–11:15). Noted during a canary of a batch_scheduler heuristic tweak.
anya: saw it, same window. Traces are sparse — only ~40% of requests have spans. Dashboard shows batch_size metric roughly unchanged which is weird.
infra-bot: deploy: batch-scheduler v2.4.3 promoted to canary (hosts: gs-rt-canary-4) at 11:02:46 :rocket:
marta: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.92 -> 0.65 around 11:03. Host gs-rt-canary-4 saw a CPU spike and >50% IO wait. Could be hot-shard eviction.
devon: I pulled flamegraphs and a short profile from the canary host. Kernel-selection path added latency and queueing increased. Snippet of relevant logs:
```
[11:03:12] kernel_selector: selected kernel int8-opt for model xlm-6b
[11:03:12] kernel_selector: fallback path: compile_jit took 180ms
[11:03:13] batch_scheduler: queue_depth=78 batch_size=4 avg_latency=680ms
[11:03:14] kvcache: evict key=uid:12345 shard=7 reason=no-space
```
leo: That `compile_jit 180ms` is suspicious — kernel compilation shouldn't happen in steady-state, we cache compiled kernels. Why did it recompile in prod?
sanjay: I checked metrics — kernel_cache_miss_ratio on gs-rt-canary-4 spiked to 0.27 at 11:03. We do not surface that metric on the per-route dashboard (observability gap).
marta: Also the traces that do exist drop spans after `runtime.request` — looks like instrumentation was suppressed during GC or high load. Missing spans make root-cause harder to pinpoint.
anya: Our logs were sampled at 1% for requests during deploys — lost a lot of fidelity. Ops alerts fired because of sampled latency metric but the traces/logs we need weren't captured. :warning:
opsbot: Alert: latency-p95-exceeded on runtime-serving-prod (11:04 -> 11:16).
leo: Temporary reproducer: small batch sizes + toggling quant config to force kernel selection churn. But first we need higher trace coverage.
devon: Mitigation attempt: rolling back the canary batch-scheduler heuristic. Executing now.
infra-bot: rollback: batch-scheduler v2.4.2 re-promoted to canary hosts at 11:07:55
marta: After rollback p95 dropped back to ~55ms within ~2 minutes. KV hit-rate recovered to ~0.89. However dashboards show mismatched windows (old sampling windows vs new) so the graph looks noisy — another observability mismatch.
sanjay: Proposed action items:
- Add `kernel_cache_miss_ratio` to per-route & per-host dashboards
- Increase trace sampling to 10% during canary windows (and auto-escalate on p95 anomalies)
- Audit kernel cache eviction TTL/size and bias for canaries to pin caches
- Surface `compile_jit` timings as a trace span so it shows up even when sampling is low
anya: Also add a quick smoke-run (100 synthetic requests with small batch sizes) to canary job to catch kernel compiles before promotion.
leo: I'll open a postmortem and attach logs. Anyone else seeing similar patterns in dedicated-prod or other regions?
marta: I saw a smaller bump on a dedicated-prod host at 11:09 but it resolved faster. May be related but less kernel churn there.
devon: Saved logs/flamegraphs to /mnt/tmp/rt-incident-1954321987.tar.gz — will attach to the PM.
leo: TL;DR — canary heuristic triggered kernel churn + KV hot-shard evictions -> compile_jit + queueing caused p95 spike. Observability gaps (trace sampling low, missing kernel metrics on dashboards) slowed diagnosis. Action items above. :clipboard:
